chapter_title: Concerning the Wheel that exists in front of the K

1.original: [of the King of Honour who dwells in]
1.content: of the King of Honour who dwells in

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** The universal ordering of Divine Providence that stands before [GAP-1: the Divine Good governing through truth, which dwells in] the complete fullness of the interior heavens [GAP-2: ...], the hidden origin of all dominant persuasions in higher and lower degrees of the mind, held fast in a great and unyielding restraint of divine order; for the entire purpose of the Divine Good that governs [GAP-3: is invested in this ordering]. Likewise, all the opposition of evil and falsity that pervades the separated states of understanding is [GAP-4: ...] and held captive within it.

**¶2:** This ordering exists in the radiance of Divine Wisdom [GAP-5: clothed in] the forms of heavenly arrangement and the beauty of spiritual perfection. Now, there are twelve constraining truths within it — truths of faith in their fullness. Each constraining truth stands between every separated state of understanding, and the dominant persuasions that dwell there [GAP-6: ... ...] are bound within it; for should any false persuasion seek to break free from divine order, it will be held fast [GAP-7: ...]. Should it attempt deception against its restraint, [GAP-8: ... it will be] made manifest and laid open in [GAP-9: that] ordering of Providence [GAP-10: ...]. All knowledges of good and truth, all insights of the heavens, and [GAP-11: the] ruling intelligence over every spiritual power exist there and are discerned through it, before the Divine Good that governs.

**¶3:** The twelfth and completing constraining truth within this ordering consists of five illuminated faculties of perception, which are joined together and interwoven throughout the entire boundary of external life; because every state in which these perceptions are constricted, and every state in which they have freedom, is made visible through this ordering of Providence. For the hidden origin of all separated states of understanding, higher and lower, together with that of their dominant persuasions, is held captive and fixed within it.

**¶4:** The spiritual vigilance [GAP-12: ...] is maintained at all times before the Divine Good that governs [GAP-13: ... ...], so that the holy dread wh[GAP-14: ich ...] will subdue all the powers where good and evil are commingled [GAP-15: ... ...] their hidden origin fastened there, so that they cannot break free from the restraint of their divinely imposed bond.

**¶5:** This ordering of Providence resembles, in this respect, a connected series of truths set before the presiding principle of spiritual watchfulness, for when [GAP-16: ...] in th[GAP-17: ose ...] in the [GAP-18: ... connected series of constraining] truths.

**¶6:** This is likewise the case for all dominant persuasions that inhabit the separated states of understanding, and every power operating through the boundary of external life: should they seek to break free, they shall be recognized and exposed through this ordering of Providence. [GAP-19: For] this ordering is like a great capacity for self-reflection through Divine Truth, by which [the di]scernment of all interior states [GAP-20: ... is] contained within it.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: the wheel that exists in front [of the King of Honour who dwells in] the seventh firmament [...], the root of the rulers above and below in a great and cruel fetter; as the entire will of the great King of Honour is placed in [it]. Also, their entire enmity, which is in the firmaments, is [bound] and ensnared in it.

It exists in a blaze of splendour [with] ornamentation and great beauty. Now, there are twelve seals in it. The seal between i[s] every firmament and the rulers who are there [... ...] are in it; for should one of them wish to escape, he will be bound [by the seal]. If he should wish to cause a trick in his bond [it will be] apparent and known in [that] wheel [before him]. The spheres and stars and [the] leader of all the powers exist there, and can be known by it, in front of the King of Honour.

The twelf[t]h seal that is in it is its five shining men that are conjoined and enmeshed through the entire zone; because every place where they are cramped, and every place where they have space, is displayed by that wheel. For the root of all the firmaments above and below, and that of their rulers, is ensnared and fixed in it.

The observation [of the wheel] is set right at all times opposite the great King o[f Honour ...] so that fear, wh[ich comes from it] will assume all the powers of mixture [... ...] their root affixed there, so that they cannot make an esc[a]pe from the fetter of their bond.
That wheel rese[m]bles, in this respect, a chain in front of the chief guard, for when [...] in th[ose fetters] in the [great cha]in.

This is also the case for all the rulers who are in the firmaments, and every power of the zone: If they should wish to escape, they shall be recognised and revealed by that wheel. [For] the wheel is like a great mirror, for [the di]scrimination of all things [that exist is] in it.

fills.fill: of the King of Honour who dwells in
fills.original: of the King of Honour who dwells in
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading confirms this is the Divine Good governing through truth dwelling in the inmost heaven; "King of Honour" is the Kephalaia's standard title for this divine principle, and "who dwells in the seventh firmament" is the established formula for his location.

The spiritual reading confirms "is invested in this ordering," and "it" is the pronoun referring to the wheel, which is the antecedent throughout the passage; the entire will of the King of Honour is placed in the wheel.

The spiritual reading indicates a term parallel to "held captive," and "bound and ensnared" is a natural doublet in Kephalaia restraint vocabulary, matching the chapter's pervasive language of fettering and binding.

The spiritual reading says "clothed in," and "with" is the natural Coptic-to-English preposition linking "a blaze of splendour" to "ornamentation and great beauty," indicating accompaniment or adornment.

The paragraph describes the twelve seals as the active constraining mechanisms between firmaments; if a ruler tries to escape, it is the seal standing between each firmament that binds him, making "by the seal" the contextually determined agent of binding.

The spiritual reading confirms "it will be made manifest," where "it" refers to the trick; the sentence requires a subject and auxiliary verb to connect "cause a trick in his bond" to "apparent and known in that wheel."
The spiritual reading confirms the demonstrative pronoun "that" before "ordering of Providence"; "that wheel" is the consistent demonstrative reference to the wheel throughout the chapter.

This mirrors the closing phrase of ¶2 ("in front of the King of Honour") and ¶1's framing of the wheel as set before the King; the trick becomes apparent in the wheel before the King who observes through it.

The spiritual reading confirms the definite article "the" before "ruling intelligence over every spiritual power"; "the leader of all the powers" requires a definite article as a specific cosmic title.

The spiritual reading indicates "spiritual vigilance" of the ordering of Providence; "the observation of the wheel" identifies the wheel as the instrument of vigilance, consistent with the chapter's theme that the wheel is set before the King of Honour for continual observation.

Completing "which comes from it" — the fear/dread that emanates from the wheel of Providence; the wheel as a divine instrument radiates holy dread that subdues the powers of mixture, consistent with the chapter's teaching that the wheel is the active restraining mechanism.

Completing "those fetters" — the chain analogy requires the specific restraint terminology; "fetter" is the chapter's primary term for individual restraints (¶1: "great and cruel fetter," ¶4: "fetter of their bond"), and "fetters" is the natural term for restraints attached to a chain before a guard.

Completing "great chain" — "great" is the chapter's consistent modifier for cosmic instruments and restraints ("great and cruel fetter," "great King," "great beauty," "great mirror"), and "in the great chain" parallels "in a great and cruel fetter" from ¶1.

The spiritual reading specifies "For" as a causal connector; "For the wheel is like a great mirror" provides the reason why rulers are recognized, and avoids the redundancy of "As the wheel is like" (double comparison), which is a stronger correction than the editor's "As."

The spiritual reading says "the discernment of all interior states ... is contained within it"; "the discrimination of all things that exist is in it" completes the statement that the wheel-mirror contains the capacity to discern everything that exists, with "discrimination" as the singular subject governing "is."
